Automatic: PyExamine with default thresholds run by script on each file/repository; cloc for TLoC. Manual: audit of flagged instances to check PyExamine precision (FE and PSS found to give false positives); manual inspection of failed solutions. Statistics: Spearman rho and Kruskal-Wallis H

Criterion: none stated by the authors; quality and cost verdicts for every entry: no criterion stated by the authors. One generation per problem. Exp. I values: Long Method (LM) counts over 90 problems, Zero-Shot / Structural (Tables 1-2):
- Direct API + Gemini-2.5-Pro, Zero-Shot (baseline prompt): LM 5; Structural: LM 8
- Direct API + Llama 3.3 (70B), Zero-Shot: LM 0; Structural: LM 0
- Direct API + DeepSeek-Coder v2 (16B), Zero-Shot: LM 2; Structural: LM 2
- Direct API + Qwen3-Coder (30B), Zero-Shot: LM 7; Structural: LM 7
- Direct API + Qwen3-Coder (480B), Zero-Shot: LM 11; Structural: LM 13
- Human baseline (one verified CodeContest submission per problem): LM 1, Temporary Field 4 (TF 0 for all LLMs)
Exp. II:
- MetaGPT + Qwen3-Coder (480B), 20 repositories: most prevalent smells TMB, PAU, UD, SF, RFC (counts only in Fig. 1 box plots); TLoC vs smells rho = 0.53 (code), 0.59 (structural), 0.94 (architectural)

Exp. I: 90 randomly sampled CodeContest problems; 5 models x 2 prompt conditions; baseline: Zero-Shot prompt and human solutions; held constant: problems and detection tool/thresholds; acceptance tests: none used in the analysis; repetitions: one generation each; no iterative debugging. Exp. II: one framework and one model; prompts constant in form, complexity varied over 4 stages for 5 scenarios; no baseline or alternative framework; factors analysed with Kruskal-Wallis (scenario, stage) and Spearman (ToF, TLoC, ALpF). Human intervention: none

Exp. I: structural prompting gave no improvement: LM rose for Qwen3-Coder 480B (11 to 13) and Gemini-2.5-Pro (5 to 8); humans show Temporary Field (4) absent in LLM code, LLMs more Long Method (Qwen3-Coder 480B 11 vs human 1); no significance tests (raw counts). Exp. II (Table 3): TLoC correlates with architectural smells rho = 0.94 (p < 0.001), structural 0.59 (p = 0.007), code 0.53 (p = 0.017); ToF with architectural 0.72 (p < 0.001), not with code (0.33, p = 0.153) or structural (0.06, p = 0.804); ALpF with structural 0.57 (p = 0.009), not with code (0.23, p = 0.329) or architectural (0.30, p = 0.201); scenario affects architectural smells (H = 9.86, p = 0.043), not code (H = 6.83, p = 0.145) or structural (H = 8.51, p = 0.075); stage (requirement specificity) has no effect (p = 0.840-0.955)

Exp. I distinguished smell profiles of humans vs LLMs but only via raw counts, one run, no statistics; two smell types (FE, PSS) found unreliable in this context. Exp. II gave significant correlations on 20 repositories. Limitations stated: no validate-and-correct loop; dependence on PyExamine default thresholds (mitigated by identical rules for all cohorts); 90-problem sample; MetaGPT only

Limitations: no iterative debugging loop in Exp. I (first-pass generation only); PyExamine thresholds; sample of 90 problems; single multi-agent framework (MetaGPT), results may be specific to its SOP paradigm; newer tools (Spec Kit, Cursor Composer) not covered. Gaps / future work: architecturally-aware agents (explicit 'Architect' role or constitutional AI), refactoring agents for AI-specific smells, longitudinal benchmarks of continuous software evolution, metrics for semantic cohesion

Inconsistencies: Exp. I sample is 'randomly sampled' (p. 4) but a 'stratified sample ... balanced across difficulty levels' in the threats (p. 9); model named 'Llama 3.3(70b)' in text but 'Llama3(70b)' in Tables 1-2; RQ mapping differs between the introduction (taxonomy = RQ2, complexity = RQ3) and the start of Section 4 (complexity = RQ2, taxonomy = RQ3); claim that 'running code is just as likely to be structurally flawed as failed code' and that 'statistical analysis confirms' prompting does not mitigate decay are not backed by reported functional data or Exp. I statistics; ALpF undefined; Agent Action Count logged but not reported. Tables 1-2 are garbled in the extracted text, only LM and TF values used (stated in text). Table 3 is also jumbled: the ToF and ALpF rows (code / structural / architectural) were rebuilt from the cell order; the TLoC, ToF-architectural, scenario and stage values are confirmed by the text (p. 8-9). Replication package on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.19245562) with sample code, prompts and generated repositories. No pre-registration. Programming language: Python
